guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.cons:
You can break blocks supplied by builders before handover, in Survival or Creative. Explosions and ordinary environmental destruction can remove them too. Until the project is physically finished, these construction-owned blocks yield no normal block loot or mining experience. This rule covers only supplied blocks, not every block in a large surrounding lot. Breaking a wall to get out is allowed.

Builders revisit missing blocks in a finishing pass. If a missing support prevents more work, it can be repaired sooner. Repairs use the construction system; they do not take items from your inventory, charge your Bank Cash or require you to rebuild the blueprint. Repeated damage can delay handover, but cannot create a stream of free replacement-block drops. The building must still pass physical inspection before it awards completed-building services.

Other safe work can continue around an occupied cell, while structural supports and construction phases still apply. Builders never place solid blocks through players or living creatures or remove their footing. If the last required cells are occupied, the report identifies the waiting location. Move yourself or guide the creature to a clear route. The mod does not teleport players or pets, delete animals or falsely finish a blocked building.

Optional yard decorations are different from required structure. If a never-built fence, trim or ornament cannot obtain its planned support because that foot was skipped on unsuitable terrain, builders leave that decoration out and continue immediately. They do not wait for an impossible cosmetic support, force floating blocks into place or replace foreign terrain. Required safety fixtures and supplied unfinished blocks are not waived by this rule.

For genuine support waits, the progress report and /emerald debug identify the waiting block, expected nearby support and its current block or unloaded state. Keep required chunks loaded and the work cells clear. An elapsed-time override cannot safely bypass a player, protected chest or missing required structure.

New construction chests and barrels remain empty and unavailable until handover. Breaking one drops neither the chest nor initial loot, and builders can replace it. Menus and ordinary hopper insertion/extraction are locked while the site is unfinished. Initial loot is granted once at handover, not once per replacement. Pistons cannot export reserved construction blocks, falling construction material cannot become harvestable blocks elsewhere, and Endermen cannot carry it away.

Leave reserved blueprint cells clear until completion: normal block placement there is refused before consuming the item. This avoids silently deleting your supplied blocks or containers during repair. Unrelated existing chests and their contents are never enrolled or erased. If an administrator or another mod has supplied contents to a construction chest, those contents take priority over the no-drop rule and are preserved rather than discarded; they are never replenished. Fluids, existing foreign blocks and external land protection can still require an obstruction to be cleared.

After handover, normal drops and container use return. You can remodel or demolish; the building will not regenerate harvested material or refill its containers. Economic payment alone is not handover. On older saves, ongoing projects can adopt their matching non-container prefix, while existing containers keep their contents and receive no second starting-loot grant. Old Manual Repair records are ambiguous: they may describe an already-finished remodel. They are not automatically enrolled in rebuilding. Ask the server operator to inspect the debug report before restoring that authority.

guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.dist:
The district map displays saved building sites and explored terrain without force-loading chunks. New natural villages show irregular, non-overlapping territory outlines, their original centers, their Bank and planned, building, completed or blocked projects. Nearby registered natural villages appear separately so you can see the shared boundary. Legacy villages retain their old survey rectangles; those were observation areas, not exclusive territory.

Drag to pan, scroll to zoom, and use Fit page or Focus to return to the relevant area. Large collections of sites and outline segments are paged to keep network updates bounded. Hover a building for its type, position and construction progress. A territory is a building-planning area, not a player land claim or proof that all of its chunks are currently loaded.

Previously sampled terrain is saved locally and remains available after its chunks unload. Checkered cells mean unknown or still-loading map data. Unsampled land stays unknown. Construction still needs actual loaded chunks and fresh safety checks, even when the map has cached terrain for that location. A high building percentage does not bypass final inspection. Optional unsafe decorations can be omitted; necessary floors, supports, entrances and facilities must pass.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.guar:
If you also install a compatible Guard Villagers edition for your Minecraft version and loader, its guards can support the village's Safety. Neither mod is required by the other. Installing the mod alone grants nothing: eligible guards must actually be nearby. TES never creates, equips, commands or consumes guards. Their own mod still controls combat, patrols and following.

By default, each eligible guard adds two temporary Safety points, up to twelve per district. Three guards give +6; six give +12; additional guards do not increase that bonus. Final Safety is still capped at 100, so a village with base Safety 95 and a +12 bonus displays 100, not 107. This is a modifier to the Safety used by growth and production, not extra residents, housing, money or instant construction. Raids, casualties and food requirements still matter.

The loaded village census looks within 48 blocks of the saved district center, including at most 24 blocks vertically. Living adult guards with active AI qualify unless they are currently targeting a player, villager, iron golem or another guard. A guard riding another entity or sealed in a tiny cell does not qualify: a bounded local check must find room to patrol at least three blocks away. This does not guarantee access to every building. Each guard is assigned to its nearest saved district; when another district observes the same guard, its old district loses that guard's credit immediately. A guard following you far from every village stops contributing on the next complete local census, or when its old observation expires. Renaming another mob to Guard does not qualify.

Hover the Town summary to see the last observed count and bonus. With default settings the census runs about every 20 seconds at 20 TPS. Unloaded chunks are unknown: they are never forced to load, and a partial survey does not erase the last observation. Without another observation, the bonus fades over seven economic days. Reopening the world starts with no cached bonus until guards are observed again, which also prevents a removed mod from leaving permanent protection.

Settings contains an integration toggle, Safety per guard (0–10), and a maximum bonus (0–30). Defaults are enabled, 2 and 12. Applying settings clears the old observation and a later loaded census recalculates it. Repeated scans replace the observation; they never keep adding points to permanent Safety.

guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.live:
Open an investment and choose 1 Day. Today is the default: the line grows with actual server quotes, about once every 15 real seconds at normal tick speed. Every player and Exchange Desk uses these tradable prices, not cosmetic animation. An order uses the quote when the server executes it, which may differ from the last screen refresh. The ordinary spread and transaction safety checks still apply.

The horizontal reference is the previous economic close. Green means the latest point is above it, red below, and grey unchanged. Unobserved time remains empty on the right of the chart. Hover a point for its economic day, time and price. Switch to Yesterday to review the previous session; its return is labeled in the graph. The Now price beneath it remains the current tradable quote and today's change. Reviewing history never changes the execution price.

A new installation or mid-day upgrade has only observations collected since then. A partial opening session says First observed instead of Previous close, and the daily percentage stays unknown until a full opening baseline exists. Yesterday may initially be unavailable. Reopening or restarting cannot invent missing observations.

Smaller steps divide drift by elapsed time and volatility by the square root of elapsed time. They do not award a full day of growth eighty times. The positive long-run fundamental targets remain a bias, not a guarantee; stocks, commodities and their derived indices can lose value.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.mark:
Use the same investment range cycle in the main chart and Compare: 1 Day, 30 Days, 90 Days, 1 Year, 3 Years, 5 Years, 10 Years, All. A year means 365 economic days. Today and Yesterday retain detailed intraday quotes; longer ranges use daily closes and the latest current quote. Home account-value and physical Trade charts remain daily samples, not intraday account-performance records.

The save retains ten years of daily closes plus a bounded older archive whose samples become farther apart as it grows. All includes those older observations, but cannot show every old fluctuation. Charts also sample points to fit the screen. History available since Day X identifies the selected series' real starting point: a young world cannot show ten years, and an upgrade cannot recover observations an older build already discarded.

Compare uses matching timestamps and starts both prices at 100 on their first common observation. Solid blue and dashed amber distinguish the investments even when both rise or fall. A new listing shortens their shared history. These are price returns, not your personal profits after spreads, deposits, withdrawals or other account flows.

Chart lines are sampled price history, not total return or a forecast. The concise point hover shows only the recorded date/time and price. Definitions, sampling limits and index construction belong here in the handbook; transaction hovers retain the amounts, destinations, fees and penalties needed before confirming an action.

The economic calendar only moves forward. Ordinary play, sleeping through the night and forward time commands advance it. Overlapping game, sky-clock and enabled wall-clock time is counted once. Savings interest, maturities, village simulation and daily news still settle once per completed economic day; faster quotes do not multiply those rewards.

An explicit backward time command means move forward to the next occurrence of the requested sky time. Market Day 23 at midnight followed by /time set 0 becomes Day 24 at dawn, not Day 0. Setting exactly the same time again adds nothing. Multiple different commands in one tick are handled individually. If offline progress separated the clocks, an explicit change aligns economic time of day forward; it never erases priced time. This also applies in Creative mode. Tiny clock differences within the same fifteen-second quote interval are kept rather than adding an extra day.

Large jumps use bounded batches. Trades and money actions wait until catch-up finishes, preventing purchases at stale pre-jump prices. The existing safety limit accepts at most 25,000 days of pending catch-up; extreme jumps beyond it are capped. Normal reloads preserve quotes and partial progress. A passive backward clock observation from a restored world is rebased without replaying old days.

Pausing or slowing the sky clock does not freeze the economy while server ticks continue: game time remains a forward-only fallback. A faster sky clock advances the economy faster. Single-player pause stops server ticks. Optional offline progression remains controlled by server settings. Administrator commands advance simulation, not promise favorable returns.

guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.reci:
To mark your own building site, use a crafting table. Place Stick, Yellow Dye, Stick across one row, then Stick, Black Dye, Stick directly below it. Four sticks and the two dyes make four construction fences. The diagram shows the exact arrangement and output; acquiring a stick reveals the recipe in the recipe book.

Recognize a construction fence by its yellow post cap, dark foot and stepped black-and-yellow rails. The same appearance is used for the fence item, straight runs, corners and junctions. These fences connect to other caution fences and have a real collision barrier. Place as many as you want for decoration or to mark an area, leaving a way in. A manually placed fence stays where you put it and drops one fence when broken in Survival. It does not reserve land, assign workers, or tell the village to build there; use the village's project and district controls for development.

Automatic construction sites supply their own temporary fences without charging your inventory. Those owned segments do not drop items, so they cannot be harvested for free fences. They disappear when the work ends and restore eligible displaced plants. Your manually placed barriers are not part of that cleanup.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.crea: Creative inventory: blocks and spawn eggs

Open the Creative inventory and find The Emerald Standard tab, marked by an Exchange Desk. It gathers the Starter Handbook, Exchange Desk, Construction Fence, Banker Villager Spawn Egg, and Builder Villager Spawn Egg in one place. You can also search for their names. The mod automatically includes future registered items in this tab, so new content will not be hidden in an unrelated category.

The two eggs are Creative tools, not Survival recipes. The Banker egg creates a villager with the Banker profession. You can talk to it for personal banking, but placing one does not create a bank building, repair an unsafe bank, claim an existing Bank, or replace its official Banker. A vanilla spawner only remembers an entity type, not a profession, so the Banker egg refuses to configure spawners. Place it on ordinary ground instead.

The Builder egg creates a persistent, unassigned builder wearing biome-matched villager clothes and a leather work apron, carrying an iron-headed hammer. It wanders and looks around but does not begin placing blocks or take over an automatic crew. These decorative/test builders are not residents, do not consume village food or housing, and do not disappear when a nearby project finishes. Remove them yourself if no longer wanted. Automatic crews still arrive, work and leave according to their assigned construction site.

The desk, handbook and fence retain Survival crafting recipes shown above. Existing worlds do not receive any extra mobs merely because the eggs were added. A current handbook opens the current guide text; use the Crafting recipes chapter again after an update to learn about new items and changed behavior.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.cons:
When a normal project starts, necessary terrain preparation happens first. The mod then establishes the eligible construction perimeter before it starts the main structural build. Fence preparation is processed in small batches to limit server work; after that, the site uses your construction speed setting, normally two block operations per second per site. Faster forced-development debugging skips new decorative crews and fences.

A perimeter is not a perfectly sealed wall. Entrance gaps, unsafe ground, protected land and overlapping active sites are intentional exclusions. Unloaded chunks and occupied fence positions wait for a later attempt. Removing a prepared fence yourself does not make the crew rebuild it forever. Do not use caution tape as a security guarantee for villagers.

Small sites receive one builder, with two, three or four for larger footprints. They try to arrive from safe loaded ground out of players' view and walk to work spots. Each worker keeps a separate, spaced position outside the building footprint and faces the nearby wall or foundation. Workers keep useful routes instead of circling between stations on a timer. If a work position becomes blocked, they try another reachable spot. Their individually phased hammering animation follows active work once they reach their station; it does not create extra blocks or speed up paid labor. If no safe unseen arrival or route is available, the crew waits; construction is not permanently blocked just because an actor cannot reach it. Exact visibility can differ with third-person cameras or freecam mods.

Builders wear Minecraft villager work clothes and a toolsmith-style leather apron instead of modern safety gear. Their outfit uses the worksite biome's vanilla villager style: plains, taiga, desert, savanna, snow, jungle or swamp. It is chosen once and saved, so walking across a biome border or reloading does not change it. Existing builders adopt a local outfit when loaded; Creative egg builders use their spawn biome. Native villager textures follow your resource pack. Their independent arms hold the iron-headed hammer fore-and-aft so its striking faces follow the up-and-down swing. The apron is cosmetic, not a trading profession.

A brief interruption stops hammering without immediately replacing the crew. After about ten seconds of continued paused, disabled or blocked work, automatic builders head away and disappear only when sufficiently distant and out of players' view. They may remain visible longer if you watch or follow them. The fence and saved construction plan stay in place. Resuming work allows arrivals after departing workers release their slots; unloaded workers keep their slots to prevent duplicates. Arrival still needs a safe loaded route and an unseen position.

After completion, assigned workers leave and the surviving owned fences are removed. Eligible grass, flowers and other plants displaced specifically for fencing are restored only where they can still survive. New player blocks are never overwritten. Trees and built structures are not removed simply to fit a fence. Manually placed fences and builders from Creative eggs have no automatic assignment, so they stay until you remove them.

guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.firs:
The Emerald Standard gives you two things to look after: your own emerald account and a living village economy. You can use either without mastering the other. Start by finding a village in the Overworld and spending a little time nearby so the mod can discover its residents and plan its Bank. A Bank may still be under construction when you arrive.

Right-click a Banker or an Exchange Desk to open the interface. If you would rather start banking immediately, craft your own desk using the visual recipe in Crafting recipes. Your personal account follows you between desks in the same world; moving to another village does not start a new balance. Town and Fund, however, describe the local settlement linked to that access point.

For a first visit, open Home to see your account, then Town to understand the village. Look at residents versus housing, Food and Safety before giving money away. A crowded village needs room to grow; a hungry one needs food support and working farms. You do not have to repair every number at once.

You can leave ordinary emeralds in your inventory and spend them directly in the GUI. Depositing first is optional. When you are ready to help, read The Village Fund, choose a small gift you can afford to lose permanently, and watch the village over several economic days. This handbook explains what to look for rather than asking you to guess what a button does.

Suppose you arrive with 320 emeralds in your inventory and no Bank Cash. You can open Fund, choose Direct Grant and a purpose, enter 100, and prepare that contribution without visiting the deposit screen. Check the preview and confirm the gift. Your remaining inventory will be 220 emeralds if there was no Bank Cash to use.

The same combined balance can fund investments, Savings deposits, CDs and villager lending. Bank Cash pays first, and inventory covers only the shortage. If you have 2.25 E in cash and spend 5 E, the desk takes three inventory emeralds and leaves 0.25 E in cash as change. Savings is separate and is never spent automatically.

Depositing is still useful when you want to free inventory space or keep loose emeralds in your account. In Bank's account-transfer view, choose an amount and Deposit. Withdrawing reverses that route for whole emeralds, subject to space in your inventory. Neither depositing nor withdrawing is investment profit.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.amou: Choose an amount, then choose the action

The amount box is a draft, not a payment. Type a whole number, press Apply to select it, and then use the action you actually want: Invest, Deposit, Support Village, or the relevant product button. The preview tells you which balance or items will be used. Cancel clears the draft; it does not reverse a transaction already completed.

All uses the source available to the current action. For a gift or investment that includes ordinary inventory emeralds plus cash; for a withdrawal it means Bank Cash, not your Savings or holdings. Exact typed amounts that have become unaffordable are rejected rather than silently changed into smaller payments. Preset actions can use up to the available amount.

Some irreversible or risky actions ask for confirmation. Read the amount, destination and purpose again before accepting. If you change the gift type, purpose or amount, check the new preview rather than treating an earlier confirmation as permission for the new action. Requests are checked on the server, and repeated clicks do not bypass the transaction cooldown.

A risky confirmation belongs to the specific position and terms you reviewed. If a selected CD disappears, Sell All holdings or price changes, or an All lending amount changes, the Desk asks you to confirm the updated action again. It does not quietly substitute the next CD or carry your old approval over to a different sale.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.risk: Choose what the money is for

Keep everyday spending money accessible before locking it away or putting it at risk. Bank Cash is your account's spending balance. Savings is a liquid, interest-bearing balance: you can move it back to cash when needed, and it does not trade at a fluctuating share price.

A CD exchanges flexibility for a fixed rate over a stated term. You can close it early, but the penalty means it is not a substitute for cash you need tomorrow. A market investment is different again: its sale value can rise or fall, so even a low-risk listing can lose emeralds. Owning several companies spreads exposure but does not remove the risk of a broad downturn.

Villager lending means you are the lender. You may receive repayment and interest, only part of your principal, or nothing. The village does not send you a debt bill if the loan fails. A Village Fund contribution is not a loan at all: it is a final gift with no repayment, interest or ownership claim.

Try unfamiliar products with a small amount first. Use the preview, term, risk description and Log to understand the result. These are game economy mechanics, not a guarantee that waiting longer or helping a village will make every investment profitable.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.acco: Read your account without mixing up balances

Home brings together your account value and history. Bank Cash is available for spending or withdrawal. Savings, investment holdings, CDs and lending positions are separate places your money can be held; their values are not all immediately withdrawable as loose emeralds.

Net Worth measures the account, not everything you own in Minecraft. Loose inventory emeralds, blocks in chests and Village Fund gifts are excluded. A deposit therefore increases recorded account value even though it only moved money you already owned. Do not mistake that increase for an investment gain.

Holdings show the shares you own and their current marked value. Cost basis tracks the purchase cost still assigned to those shares. Average buy price is that remaining cost divided by the shares held. Unrealized gain or loss describes a holding you have not sold; realized gain or loss describes an exit that has already occurred.

Use the history and Log together when a number surprises you. Moving cash to Savings is an internal transfer, while withdrawing items or giving money to the village takes value out of your account. Your account is personal and shared across desks in this world; the village treasury is not your wallet.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.mone: Know where a transaction ends up

Ordinary emeralds in your main inventory, hotbar and offhand can cover GUI spending. Renamed or otherwise customized emeralds are protected, and the desk does not reach into shulker boxes, bundles or other nested storage. Items held on the mouse cursor and emerald blocks are not loose spending emeralds.

Market sales, resource exchanges, CD payouts and collected loan repayments go to Bank Cash. They do not automatically fill your inventory. Move Savings back to cash if you want to spend that balance; selling investments or closing a CD is a separate decision with its own price or penalty.

A successful inventory top-up is saved before the purchase or gift it funds. If the later action fails, the top-up stays safely in Bank Cash; it is not a second charge. Check the message and balances before trying again. For persistent recovery warnings, see Help and recovery rather than moving items between saves.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.mark:
Open Mkt and browse the listings with the arrows or selection control. Read the investment type, description and risk before choosing an amount. Invest buys fractional shares or commodity units at the current execution terms using cash and, if necessary, ordinary inventory emeralds. You do not need enough emeralds for one whole share.

The graph shows recorded price history over the selected period. A new world or newly added listing may have little or no history; leave economic time to advance before expecting a useful chart. The green or red price change is a description of past movement, not a prediction of the next day.

A small trading spread makes buying and immediately selling costly even if the displayed market price has not moved. Use the sale preview to see the expected proceeds. Sell 25%% reduces the selected holding; Sell All exits it. The proceeds return to cash and can then be spent or withdrawn.

Market conditions, company-specific behavior and events all matter. Village activity can contribute a bounded influence, but a prosperous Town does not force all shares upward. Reopening the screen or reloading the world does not reroll the seeded market.

The selector labels each listing Stock, Index, Fund, or Commodity. A stock represents a business, VILX is the diversified index, and TREA is a treasury fund. AURM is a gold-reserve company stock; it is different from GOLD, which tracks gold itself.

Commodity investments include Gold, Iron, Coal, Diamond, Copper, Redstone, Lapis Lazuli, and Netherite Scrap. They are cash-settled price holdings, not items delivered to your inventory. Buy fractional units with emeralds and sell them back for Bank Cash. One GOLD unit follows one gold ingot's base quote; NETH follows scrap, not a crafted netherite ingot. Where Trade supports the resource, both tabs use the same underlying quote, with investment spreads applied on top.

Gold responds to defensive demand, iron and copper to industry and rebuilding, coal to fuel demand, redstone to automation, lapis to enchanting expeditions, and diamond and netherite to their own markets. Different supply shocks and volatility make these alternatives, not guaranteed profits or company shares. Trade remains the separate place to sell supported physical resources; it does not convert investment units into items.

Browse / compare opens a searchable investment directory without placing an order. Search names, tickers or sectors; the Type button cycles through Stocks, Commodities, Index and Fund. Favorites are a local watchlist saved on this computer, not an automatic trading instruction. Holdings-only checks actual ownership, even when a tiny position rounds to zero. Such positions display as <0.01 E rather than disappearing; large holdings keep their full supported value. Filters combine, so Clear search also resets them when a listing seems missing. Pin one Compare choice, then choose another to see type, risk, live quotes and holdings together. Return to the directory to select an investment, and use the ordinary reviewed Buy or Sell action. A lower unit price alone does not mean better value.

Tiny holdings still belong to you even if their displayed share count rounds to zero. Sell buttons use actual ownership. The server sells the real quantity, but refuses a sale that would pay less than the smallest cash unit (0.000001 E); it never deletes that dust merely to tidy the display. Sub-cent quotes are preserved. At extreme holding sizes, a trade is refused if numeric precision cannot represent the change safely. Your existing money and holdings remain intact.

Daily changes beside listings compare the current server quote with the previous economic close: green means up, red down, and grey means flat or not enough history. The single chart color describes its selected period, which can differ from today's direction. Percentages and signs remain visible without relying on color.

In Compare, each Details column scrolls independently under your mouse. The shared chart rebases both prices to 100 on the same first date, then overlays a solid blue line and a dashed amber line. Cycle 1 Day, 30 Days, 90 Days, 1 Year, 3 Years, 5 Years, 10 Years, then All. Returns are price changes, not forecasts or total returns after trading spreads. A new listing shortens the overlap to its real recorded history; no earlier values are invented. All combines up to ten economic years of daily closes with a bounded, coarser archive of older observed closes. Upgrading cannot restore history that an older version discarded.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.inve: Broad exposure or a particular business?

VILX is the Villager Stock Exchange Index. It tracks all twelve company stocks, including Aurum Reserve, Masons & Works, Tidewater Fisheries and Frontier Expedition Ventures. Commodities, VCIX and the Treasury Fund are not company stocks and are excluded. Buying one VILX holding gives exposure to the basket rather than requiring you to buy each business separately.

Every company starts with equal simulated market capitalization: approximately 8.33%% of the basket. Capitalization means its quoted share price multiplied by its saved simulated shares outstanding. Those company share counts are not players' holdings. As prices move, stronger companies become larger parts of VILX; it does not reset to equal weights each day or when the world reloads. Increasing concentration can make one company's problems matter more.

VILX's price comes entirely from that capitalization basket. If every constituent falls over the same period, the index falls too. If most fall but a sufficiently large company rises, VILX can still rise. News and village conditions affect companies first; the index does not receive another copy of the same effect. Stock splits change share counts and denomination, not the company's basket weight or your investment value. The former independent market component and upside limiter have been removed.

The companies keep their individual positive 1-15%% annual fundamental targets. VILX's indicative bias is their current capitalization-weighted average, not a new random target or promised return. The average stays within that range, but its probabilities differ from those of an individual company. Actual annual gains may exceed 15%%, and years or longer holding periods can lose money. There is no guaranteed recovery or year-end top-up.

For existing worlds, the upgrade preserves VILX's current quote, your units, cost basis and recorded history. Equal capitalization is established at that point using the current company prices, then weights drift from there. Earlier chart points still show the old method; they are not recalculated to pretend the new basket existed in the past. Reloading a converted save preserves the established share counts and tracking date.

The companies emphasize different sectors. Redstone Dynamics (RSDN), Deepdelve Mining (DPMN) and Nether Spice (NSPC) have stronger business-specific swings. Golden Harvest (GLDH) emphasizes agriculture, while Iron Golem Security (IRNG) emphasizes village services. Potionworks (POTN), Ender Freight (ENDR) and Minecart Transit (MCRT) cover alchemy and transport.

A sector name tells you its economic exposure, not a physical production order. Buying GLDH does not plant a field, and buying IRNG does not spawn a guard. To change the actual village, improve its surroundings or use its Fund. To change your portfolio, buy or sell shares.

VCIX is the Villager Commodity Index. It starts with equal emerald value in Gold, Iron, Coal, Diamond, Copper, Redstone, Lapis and Netherite Scrap: one eighth each, not equal numbers of physical items. After launch the weights drift as their prices move; it is not periodically reset to equal weights. VCIX has no separate growth draw or news shock. Its daily price return comes from the current weighted basket, so if every commodity falls, the index falls too. The underlying commodities keep their positive 1-15%% long-run fundamental targets, but the basket's actual return may be negative or exceed that range. In existing worlds it starts at 100 E on upgrade with no invented past chart. Your other holdings are unchanged.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.spec: Why the newer listings behave differently

Village Treasury Fund (TREA) is a lower-volatility market investment, not Savings or a CD. Income is reflected in its share price rather than paid as an extra cash dividend. Its modeled bond value tends to suffer when interest rates rise and benefit when they fall, so its price is not guaranteed.

Aurum Reserve (AURM) has defensive, partly opposite exposure to the broad market. It can benefit from recession or credit fears and lag during a strong boom. It is not redeemable for gold and does not promise to match the price of physical gold.

Masons & Works (BRCK) is more sensitive to expansion, rebuilding and credit conditions. It can move strongly in both directions. Tidewater Fisheries (FISH) adds seeded catch cycles and independent business shocks; those are simulated economic seasons, not the weather outside or the number of fish you caught.

Frontier Expedition Ventures (VENT) combines high independent volatility with rare expedition successes and failures. Large gains and losses are both possible. Different behavior is useful for variety, but it does not create a safe combination that guarantees profit.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.savi: Savings for flexibility; CDs for a planned wait

Savings earns a variable annual rate and remains liquid. Move an amount into Savings from cash or inventory when you want interest without choosing a share price. Move it back to cash before spending or withdrawing it. The rate can change with the economy; today's rate is not a promise for the whole year.

A Certificate of Deposit, or CD, fixes its opening rate for a term of 30, 90, 180 or 365 economic days. Choose the term as well as the amount, and check which position is selected before closing one. You can hold up to eight CD positions, each with its own start day and maturity.

Closing before maturity forfeits accrued interest and charges 1%% of the original principal. At maturity, closing pays the matured value into Bank Cash without that early-close penalty. A longer term is only helpful if you can leave the money there; it is frustrating to lock your village's next gift into a CD and immediately need it back.

An annual rate is quoted on a 365-economic-day basis, not a per-day reward. For example, 4%% per year does not turn 100 E into 104 E tomorrow. Interest is calculated over economic time, so use the displayed value and maturity date rather than multiplying the annual percentage by every passing day.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.lend: Lend only money you can afford to lose

Villager lending lets you finance a loan position for a term of 30, 90, 180 or 365 economic days. Select the term, choose an amount, and read the yield and risk before opening it. You can have up to eight positions, and each is tracked independently.

You are lending your emeralds, not borrowing from the Banker. The advertised return is not a guaranteed payment. When a loan resolves, it can be repaid, partly default, or fully default. A partial default returns a recovery share; a full default can lose the principal. You never owe additional debt because one of your loans failed.

Wait for the selected position to resolve and become collectible, then collect its payout into Bank Cash. Opening another loan does not overwrite an older one. Check the position's term and result instead of assuming every visible value is available to spend now.

Lending and donations solve different problems. A loan is a risky personal financial product; it is not the Fund's earmarked building budget. If your intention is to feed the Town or support a housing project, use the Village Fund instead. If your intention is to earn safe, liquid interest, compare Savings before choosing lending.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.trad:
Trade sells supported resources from your inventory to the economy. It is not a shop for buying items back. Choose the exact resource form, enter a count, Apply it, and inspect the quote before Exchange. The count means items of that selected form: one block is not one ingot.

Quotes use the mod's commodity rules and current economy, so the same count can be worth a different amount on another economic day. Read the selected item and payout together. The proceeds arrive as Bank Cash, ready for GUI spending or withdrawal.

Only ordinary supported stacks are exchanged automatically. Named or customized items are left alone. For plain loose emeralds, Deposit in Bank is the simple item-to-cash transfer; you do not need Trade merely to spend them. Keep building materials you still want before choosing All.
Check the resource form before exchanging

Diamond trading recognizes diamonds, diamond blocks, diamond ore and deepslate diamond ore. Gold trading includes ingots, raw gold, raw gold blocks, gold blocks, ordinary and deepslate gold ore, and Nether gold ore. These are separate selections with their own conversion rules.

If you want to sell a stack of raw gold, select raw gold rather than a gold ingot and verify the available count. Ore is valued by the mod's quote, not by a guarantee about what Fortune would produce after mining it. The preview is the relevant offer; decide whether to keep, process or exchange the resource before confirming.

Netherite trading supports ancient debris, scrap, ingots and blocks. Those forms are valuable in different ways for crafting, so pay particular attention to the item name and count when using All.

Emerald blocks and emerald ore, including deepslate ore, have explicit Trade selections. A block sitting in your inventory is not automatically split to pay a gift. You can craft it into loose emeralds yourself for ordinary GUI spending, or use its supported exchange route and read the quoted outcome.

A resource exchange is final once completed. The Trade screen does not offer a matching buy-back button to undo an accidental sale. If your inventory changes while the screen is open, recheck the available count and preview; an exact request that no longer fits is rejected.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.vill: Read Town as a health report, not a score to spend

Town describes the settlement linked to this desk. Status is its current condition, Residents is its population, Housing is its effective accommodation, and Development tier describes its stage of development. These are different measurements, not one pool of points.

In the example 18 / 16 housing, the village has 18 residents but effective housing for only 16. That is crowding, not 18 progress points out of a target of 16. Extra food alone will not provide the missing rooms. Keep existing beds accessible, add suitable nearby housing, or fund housing development, then allow the local census to update.

Housing is surveyed throughout the village's claimed territory, including associated mod homes and its starter area. All world heights are checked, so upper floors and hillside homes are no longer excluded by a six-block vertical limit. New natural villages use exclusive, irregular territory parcels: a bed is counted by only its owning district. Old districts retain their historical survey rules. Unloaded chunks retain their last bed observation and are never force-loaded. A cached bed is not proof that it is usable now; arrivals recheck both bed halves, occupancy, physical access and landing safety.

The resident census tracks loaded villagers by identity and saved district ownership, including tagged residents outside the surveyed territory. Breeding, curing, transported unregistered villagers and Creative eggs can add residents. A registered villager moves districts only after a confirmed home in the other district; walking across a boundary alone does not change ownership. Bankers and construction crews are not ordinary residents.

A missing resident is marked Unverified, not dead or emigrated. Their housing commitment is retained, so unloading a house cannot generate a replacement. A real death or a confirmed move is different evidence. Town's progress report separates the loaded census, unverified records, queued arrivals, immigration progress, surveyed beds and the combined city resident total. Surveys run periodically and their block work is spread across ticks; the display is not an instant head count. Natural-village districts support up to 512 simulated residents; legacy districts retain the 64-resident simulation bound. Additional actual villagers can still be observed. Up to 1,024 resident identities and 4,096 bed positions are retained per district; these are safety bounds, not growth targets.

The Food, Materials and Treasury values on the right are simulated village stocks. They are not stacks waiting in a Bank chest, and they are not your personal account. Read them alongside production and upkeep to understand whether the village can support another project.

Town opens the village overview with scores, local resources, City expansion and District map. Choose What next? Progress report when you want the resident checklist and current construction details before deciding what to fund. PASS describes one observed threshold, not guaranteed growth. The report separates planning inputs, paid economic labor and physical construction, and gives an action for common waiting states. Saved obstruction flags do not identify an exact block or prove that a player is blocking it. The origin chunk being loaded does not prove every work cell is loaded. Back or Town returns to the overview. Selecting the Town tab always starts there, even after visiting expansion or the district map.

The report lists repairs and relocation first, then active building sites, then projects searching for land. Completed simulated-only projects are not unfinished construction. At most eight waiting projects are shown, with an explicit omitted count when more exist.

The mod saves a new settler's identity before inserting its entity. If an unexpected crash happens in that tiny gap, the claim stays unverified rather than risking a duplicate. Normal failed insertions return the approval to the queue. The progress report and /emerald debug expose the queue and unverified counts; do not assume every unverified entry needs replacing.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.town:
Prosperity runs from 0 to 100 and summarizes living conditions. In ordinary difficulty, its target is built from 18 base points, up to 28 for housing coverage, up to 24 for food reserves, up to 22 for Safety, and up to eight for Development tier. Housing reaches its full contribution when effective capacity covers the population. The food contribution fills at about 30 days of the model's standard food use.

The current score moves toward that target over time: ordinarily it closes about 8%% of the remaining gap per economic day, rather than jumping straight there. Shortages, incidents and unpaid city upkeep can also reduce it. An 80.1 score is not 80 emeralds, and a 100-emerald gift does not add 100 Prosperity.

Safety is a separate 0-to-100 measure of stability. Incidents can damage it, and recovery takes time. Once the incident recovery window has passed, the simulation gradually restores Safety, helped by security output and recently observed outdoor lighting coverage. Place useful lights around routes and occupied areas; piling many torches into one already-lit spot is not an unlimited point bonus.

Security gifts do not directly buy Safety points. They supply the economy and can support Guard Post development. Defending residents, removing real threats, and maintaining useful lighting help the living settlement while those improvements take effect.
Food stocks are not Farm output

The F / M / T line means Farm, Mine and Trade output for an economic day. For example, F 25.8 means about 25.8 simulated agriculture units were produced by that day's calculation. It does not mean 25.8 farms, harvested wheat items, or points you can spend. These figures are production, not the final change in storage.

Food changes after production, resident consumption and a little spoilage. Materials gain mining output and other production, then lose maintenance and project costs. Trade output contributes only part of its value to Treasury; transport also contributes, while residents, buildings and city administration cost money.

With 18 residents on ordinary difficulty, baseline food use is about 18 x 0.46 = 8.28 units per economic day before spoilage. A Farm output near 25.8 can therefore build a reserve, but a large stock still costs a little to maintain. Peaceful uses less food and boosts productivity.

Population, professions, operational buildings, Prosperity, Safety and lifecycle all influence these production calculations. Town's Local impact is the village's bounded influence on the market, not a promise of profit. Improving a farm can help agriculture without increasing every investment by the same amount.

Young, healthy villages also mobilize limited local building supplies during their starter development drive. These supplies enter simulated Materials, Treasury and development points, not your inventory or Bank Cash. This temporary construction support is separate from the Farm / Mine / Trade output figures and does not consume Village Fund gifts.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.grow:
Development tier is a functional level from 0 to 5, not a meter filled directly by donations. The current checks look at residents, Prosperity and completed operational projects. Tier 1 needs at least five residents or an operational project. Tier 2 needs eight residents and a Warehouse. Tier 3 needs twelve residents, at least 55 Prosperity, a Warehouse and a Mine Entrance.

Tier 4 needs eighteen residents, at least 65 Prosperity and four operational projects. Tier 5 needs twenty-eight residents, at least 75 Prosperity and six operational projects. The highest qualifying tier wins. If conditions worsen, the functional tier can fall without deleting the buildings you can already see.

Development points are a separate internal planning resource produced by the economy and some Fund spending. Projects use them alongside materials and treasury. They are not player XP, donor rank or the 0-to-100 Prosperity score. Completing planning and physically placing the building are also separate stages.

Immigration now accumulates saved progress each economic day instead of a tiny daily lottery. Active or Recovering districts need spare housing, Safety of at least 45, enough food for ten units per committed resident including the proposed arrivals, and no repeated city-upkeep shortfall. Paused development also pauses immigration. Healthy small districts usually approve roughly one settler per day; larger prosperous districts can approve small groups. As an example, with 100 Prosperity and Safety, an eight-resident district earns about 1.18 arrivals/day, while a 48-resident district earns about 3.18. Peaceful increases the rate by 15%%, capped at four approvals in one day. These examples assume plenty of housing and food; recovering or strained settlements progress more slowly.

Fractions carry forward and survive reloading. New immigration approvals keep at most eight settlers waiting to appear. Older saves retain any larger already-approved queue until it drains; those commitments are not silently deleted. Full housing, a full queue or ineligible conditions cannot bank many days of arrivals for a sudden burst. New natural villages keep one district as they grow, with up to 512 simulated residents and 512 project records. Legacy districts retain their 64-resident bound. Additional actual villagers remain visible in the census, but do not increase simulated output indefinitely.

A healthy starter village now aims to prepare one or two useful projects per economic day, with faster local labor and limited construction supplies. The drive needs at least four living residents, Active status, Safety of at least 45, ten food units per resident and no city-upkeep deficit. It is strongest for the first few approved projects, tapers toward the eighth, and is weaker across larger cities. Relocating or demolishing a project does not reset that lifetime count. Need still decides what gets built; the village also prepares a modest food, security and housing cushion. This is not the unrestricted forced-development debugging mode.

Closing the world does not spawn entities. If offline catch-up is enabled, elapsed economic days can advance immigration, but the same queue and resource limits apply. Sleeping advances skipped economic time as usual. Backward time commands and reopening do not replay an arrival already approved for an economic day.

In visual play, each arrival still needs a free intact bed in surveyed district housing, clear safe standing room with a path to that bed, and loaded chunks. The default arrival attempt is about every 30 seconds at 20 TPS; a housing survey can delay it further. Nearby exposed monsters block that landing, but walls or underground terrain can shelter it. The mod never replaces a resident simply because their chunk is unloaded.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.need: Help a village with work in the world

For renewable food support, grow wheat, carrots, potatoes or beetroot around the developed district and keep livestock nearby. Riper crops count more than seedlings. Melons, pumpkins and their stems, berries, cocoa and sugar cane also contribute with different weights. Cows, mooshrooms, pigs, sheep, chickens and rabbits count as livestock; babies contribute less than adults.

The crop and livestock figures are weighted observations, so decimals are normal. More sources improve the bonus with diminishing returns, approaching a combined ceiling of +150%% before freshness adjustment. This bonus multiplies simulated Farm output; it does not spawn bread or consume an animal every day.

If you harvest everything and leave the fields empty, or kill the surrounding livestock, future loaded surveys see fewer sources and the bonus falls. Replant and keep breeding stock for a lasting benefit. Putting food in a random chest or dropping wheat on the ground is not a Village Fund donation.

Coverage grows with developed plots and their nearby field margins. Overlapping sources belong to one district rather than being counted twice. Surveys are spread out and inspect loaded chunks; cached unloaded sources are not immediately treated as destroyed, although old observations can lose freshness. Changes therefore need time to appear in Town.

For other needs, keep doors, paths and beds usable, give villagers access to appropriate workstations, and light the outdoors where they move. Use City expansion and News for the current bottleneck, then choose a Fund purpose that addresses it instead of donating blindly.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.dist:
Newly discovered natural villages have one permanent district and one Bank. The mod reads the village's loaded world-generation structure identity, so new houses, beds and Bank bells cannot repeatedly found more districts. Nearby natural villages remain separate, even when their centers are close. Natural villages added by world-generation mods are supported when their structures use Minecraft's village tag.

The district starts with its original generated houses and streets, connected to a compact rounded center area. The planner tries a rotating batch of interior sites before nearby frontier parcels. A successful, fully checked building reservation can extend the same territory with a short connected strip and its building footprint. Failed lots do not claim distant land or create outposts. The map shows the resulting irregular outline, not its enclosing rectangle.

Territories use 16-block parcels. Between known natural villages, the nearer original village center owns each parcel; UUID breaks exact ties. Expansion can continue on other sides instead of overlapping a neighbor. Undiscovered terrain is not scanned or force-loaded. Discover both nearby natural villages before comparing their shared boundary; the displayed and eligible territory is clipped when a neighboring natural village is first registered; existing buildings are not moved or deleted. These are planning boundaries, not protection claims against players.

Automatic growth still needs residents, housing demand, food, materials, treasury, safe loaded building sites and manageable upkeep. More residents can require additional granaries, warehouses, market squares and guard posts, but not another Bank for each neighborhood. Approval required lets the world owner approve a territory extension; Paused stops construction and arrivals. Debug forced development bypasses economic gates, not world safety.

A single new district can retain up to 512 projects, 512 simulated residents and 16,384 territory parcels. These are protective storage/simulation ceilings, not a promise of smooth performance at those sizes. Physical work keeps its bounded scheduler. Existing pre-update multi-district saves stay readable, and their blocks, inventories, funds and identities are not merged or deleted automatically. They no longer automatically branch into new districts. Use a fresh test world to evaluate the one-district design.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.safe:
Threatened means the village is dealing with recent incidents or very low Safety. Devastated reflects a deeply weakened settlement, such as very low Prosperity or very few survivors. Recovering is a rebuilding phase, and Active means it has returned to ordinary operation. These are lifecycle states, not different currencies.

Start by protecting the survivors and the routes they use. Deal with nearby hostiles, make entrances usable, and improve outdoor lighting. A high stock of Food is helpful, but it does not erase a recent raid or make an unsafe spawn point valid. Security funding supports development rather than replacing actual protection.

Recovery proceeds over economic days and can be slowed by another incident. A recovering settlement normally needs at least four residents, Safety 50 and Prosperity 35 to become Active again. Keep its essential supplies and housing in place while it rebuilds. Do not interpret one slow census update as proof that a villager or bed has vanished permanently.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.coll: Extinct is not the same as abandoned

An Extinct settlement has lost its resident population; an Abandoned settlement can require explicit restoration support before automatic recovery is allowed. The incident history matters, including whether the player caused the destruction. Killing the population and immediately giving emeralds back is not an instant reset.

Use Fund's Restoration purpose when the recovery message asks for it. The restoration target is 25 E actually applied to the restoration record, not 25 Prosperity or 25 E in your own wallet. Direct grants to an Abandoned or Extinct settlement are redirected to Restoration. Reaching the target still leaves recovery timing and safe physical arrivals to resolve.

When automatic recovery is enabled, the mod can queue settlers and restart a small recovering community. They need loaded, usable space, enough food and beds, with no immediate threats at the arrival site. A donation is not a command to summon villagers into danger.

If a desk reports an empty settlement while a nearby village is plainly occupied, read Help and recovery. The desk's village association and loaded census need investigation; repeatedly paying restoration at the wrong access point is not a reliable fix.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.proj:
Housing projects increase accommodation: a Cottage adds four capacity, a House six, and an Inn eight when its benefits are available. An Inn also supports trade. These are economic housing gains, not a promise that every visible bed has already been reached by a villager.

Granaries strengthen agriculture. Mine Entrances and Smithies support mining output. Warehouses, Market Squares, Inns and Exchange Halls help trade in different combinations, with several also supporting transport. Guard Posts strengthen security output. Maintaining more buildings consumes resources, so development creates ongoing needs as well as benefits.

The simulation chooses projects according to the village's condition and existing development. A Housing gift supports that category; it does not open a menu where you order an exact house on an exact block. Funding General gives broader flexibility. See The Village Fund for which purposes can finance each project family.

Layouts, building sizes and architectural details can vary. A newly founded district begins with accommodation and can develop its own neighborhood. Small public spaces and connections are part of making the settlement usable, not additional personal investment holdings.

If a saved project has no approved site, open Town > What next? Progress report. The search line shows how many candidate positions have been tried, prior failures, the retry countdown and the last observed check. A site-search cooldown is 10, 20, then at most 30 seconds at normal server speed, rather than growing to many minutes. An old long search delay is shortened when the district next becomes active. Searching the full candidate set can take longer than the cooldown; work still requires a nearby player, loaded chunks and enabled, unpaused development.

Open-looking ground is not automatically a valid building site. The complete footprint, safe terrain adjustment, entrance, protected blocks and other reserved sites must all fit. The map may display cached terrain from unloaded chunks. Do not demolish your village just because a project is searching. Run /emerald debug beside the affected district, stay nearby while it searches, then run the same command again to save the report. Candidate locations, checked orientations, rejection categories and all project retry timers are captured automatically. Checks not observed in the current session are explicitly unknown; the command does not force-load land, approve sites or accelerate construction.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.plan:
Planning (simulated) is the project's economic work. It uses the village economy and eligible funding to prepare development. Building is the physical placement work you see in the world. A planning percentage is not the percentage of roof blocks already placed, and a paid project may still have visible work left.

Direct Grants can cover the exact remaining capital or labor of an eligible selected project when fast-track funding is enabled. Sponsorship targets an active project's labor. Neither contribution bypasses protected areas, occupied blocks or the physical placement scheduler. A large donation therefore does not make every building appear immediately.

Normal construction defaults to two block changes per second per site at 20 server ticks per second. The speed is adjustable in Settings, and concurrent sites have their own allowance. Low server tick rate, unloaded chunks or a blocked placement can make observed progress slower. Construction crews, site fencing and temporary activity identify the work area; finishing the job triggers their cleanup.

Economic simulation can continue while physical work waits for its chunks to load. That distinction explains a construction backlog after time catch-up. Let the area load and give the queue time to proceed rather than breaking the unfinished desk to force another Bank.

Only two unfinished, non-repair-required development sites per district are admitted at a time, keeping the physical backlog small; Banks have their own construction queue. Finishing a site frees room for another approval. This limits simultaneous projects, not eventual city size. A protected or damaged site is not silently demolished to keep the target pace.

Sleeping through the night already advances the economic clock. It now also gives recently active construction sites a limited catch-up allowance. After waking, loaded sites can temporarily build faster in small, shared-budget batches while their saved construction plans, protection checks and entity-clearance checks still apply. The ordinary two-block rate remains unchanged outside this catch-up. Large templates, extensive terrain preparation or blocked sites can still take longer than a day.

Physical work follows a support-first sequence: approved terrain preparation, eligible caution fencing, ground foundations and floor, frame, walls, roof, then openings, furnishings and lighting. Upper-storey floors wait for the frame or masonry below. A support can cross the phase order when another part needs it. Hanging lamps wait for their attachments. This is a visual construction schedule, not a structural-engineering simulation or a perfectly sealed fence.

An unfinished project keeps its saved sequence and later upgrades append their own range. Damage during initial construction now enters an automatic finishing-repair pass rather than demanding player blueprint repairs. No-drop ownership prevents harvesting replacement blocks. Missing supports may be repaired earlier when needed to continue. Older details without an authored connection remain deferred; finished designs are not silently redesigned. Read Construction damage and handover for the precise safety and storage rules.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.terr:
The planner tries to use workable terrain and can clear ordinary vegetation such as grass, flowers, bushes and trees. Small natural irregularities do not automatically forbid a site. Foundations and approach work help connect structures to the surrounding ground, with an emphasis on accessible entrances.

Completed buildings also receive a separate walkway connection survey, including older saves. It seeks a continuous walking route to an earlier completed building entrance, or an existing village dirt path near the district center for the first connector. An arbitrary patch near the center does not count as a connection. The survey follows usable ground, detours around obstacles and verifies its center cells before recording success. Shoulders are best effort: a narrow passage is better than a wide dead end.

The survey and paving are spread over small updates. It only inspects loaded chunks, never excavates a cliff or clears a tree for a shortcut, and respects protected land, building lots, inventories and headroom. One-block grades are allowed; water and steeper steps need another route. Surveys have a 384-block endpoint-distance limit and a 512-cell route limit, with a bounded search margin. If no safe loaded route is found, it waits and retries; it cannot promise a connection through every landscape. Keep the village active and the intervening terrain loaded while it finishes. /emerald debug includes each project's connection progress and reason.

Connection receipts survive reloads. Once this pass supplies paving, it will not replace that paving if you remove it; it can try another route while still unfinished. Completed connections are left alone for player editing, and buildings themselves are never rebuilt by this finishing pass.

Completed mod-created walkways gain matching street lamps as a separate finishing pass. These use the same masonry socket, wooden post, knee brace, arm, chain and warm lantern as the village's yard lamps, with the building's saved palette. Arms face inward toward the walkway and posts alternate sides when room allows. Typical spacing is about ten path blocks; short entrance paths and already well-lit stretches do not need extra posts.

Existing completed paths can receive this lighting after updating while their village is loaded and development is enabled. The work is paced in small batches and does not alter the saved building blueprint, remove the path surface or bill your personal account. A blocked side can use the opposite verge. Reserved lots, player builds, water, steep ground and occupied cells are checked before placement; unavailable chunks wait without being loaded by the lamp system. Unsafe spots can remain unlit, so this is not a guarantee against every monster spawn.

Placed lamps have ordinary drops and remain yours to modify or remove. Saved one-shot receipts prevent the mod from repeatedly replacing harvested lamps or duplicating them where routes overlap. If a player changes a partially placed post, its remaining decoration is abandoned rather than rebuilt over those edits.

This is not permission to overwrite every obstruction. Player-build checks, built-in no-build zones, existing structures and occupancy checks still matter. Natural-looking player landscaping can be hard to distinguish from terrain, so a deliberate no-build zone is the stronger way to protect a place you care about. Server owners can use the mod's no-build commands for that purpose.

Workers temporarily defer occupied cells rather than deliberately placing a wall through a player or animal. Staying inside the unfinished footprint can therefore delay part of a project. Move outside and let it retry. Rough terrain and other mods can still expose edge cases; keep a backup and report the location rather than assuming every possible hillside is guaranteed to work.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.dama: What happens when a building is altered

Finishing a structure does not give the mod permission to endlessly overwrite your later changes. Damage checks distinguish workable structures from those that need repair, and blocked projects retry in the background where it is safe to do so. A materially damaged project can lose its economic benefits even though much of the building is still visible.

Breaking an Exchange Desk is not a general-purpose demolition command for its Bank. Bank identity, operation and replacement are separate checks. A minor edit should not be used as a method to request another building, and adding another desk does not guarantee the two access points describe the same village.

During initial construction, breaking a builder-supplied block is allowed but yields no normal drops; builders repair the missing block before handover. A temporary occupant makes the scheduler try other safe work. If only obstructed work remains, clear the reported position or guide the creature away. Existing foreign blocks, protected land and unloaded chunks remain real limits. Old Manual Repair records are not automatically rebuilt because they can also represent deliberate changes to finished buildings. Include /emerald debug, the coordinates and recent changes when reporting a persistent stall.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.fund: Give with a purpose

The Village Fund is the settlement's donated support budget. It is separate from your Bank Cash and from the village's ordinary Treasury. Money given here leaves your account permanently: it is not a deposit you can withdraw later, a loan, or shares in the village.

Begin in Town. Ask whether the real bottleneck is food, crowded housing, low Safety, slow construction or depleted Treasury. Then open Fund, choose the gift Type and Purpose, select an amount and read the confirmation. Ordinary inventory emeralds can pay the gift directly after available Bank Cash is used.

Purpose controls how the budget can be used; it does not add an equal number of points to the matching Town statistic. The following sections describe both routine spending and compatible project funding. The rates quoted are for the current model, before resource caps, and apply to money actually spent by the village, not necessarily to every emerald you just donated.

Apply an amount, then choose Preview before giving it away. This read-only report shows the selected type and actual purpose, the cash/inventory payment split, and the amount expected to enter purpose capital, emergency reserve, protected principal or project labor. It updates while open, but conditions can change before confirmation: the server checks again. The preview makes no payment. Back returns to Fund so you can review and confirm the gift.

General grants to abandoned or extinct villages are automatically routed to Restoration, even when optional targeted donations are disabled. Disabling donations or village simulation still blocks them. Preview and payment share these eligibility checks. A disabled type or missing sponsorship project is rejected before inventory emeralds are moved into Bank Cash.
Direct Grant, Endowment or Sponsorship?

A Direct Grant is usable support for current needs. Normally 20%% goes into the emergency reserve and 80%% into the selected purpose's spendable budget. That split is configurable; Restoration grants are exempt from the reserve split. Routine spending is paced by the configured budget, so an accepted gift can remain in the Fund for a while. The default ordinary budget is 24 E per 30-economic-day month, released as a shared 0.8 E daily limit, not 24 E every day. Eligible fast-track project funding is an exception to that routine limit.

An Endowment protects the donated principal and generates payouts for its selected purpose. The default payout rate is 4%% annually on a 365-economic-day basis, with the configured reserve share taken from payouts. The original principal is not spent on construction and cannot be withdrawn by the donor. It is a slow, lasting contribution, not the quickest response to today's food shortage.

Project Sponsorship is tied to an eligible unfinished project's remaining economic labor. Its purpose follows the project type rather than an unrelated selection. Extra sponsorship after the project finishes moves into the matching purpose's spendable budget; it does not come back to your account.

With fast-track capital enabled, eligible player-origin General or matching-purpose grants can cover one selected project's missing inputs and remaining labor when enough is available. Sponsorship is used first for that project's labor. This can bypass routine spending pace for that project, but not the physical build speed, protection checks, or an extreme food emergency.
General: flexible development, not a bit of everything

Choose General when you want to support the village broadly or when Treasury and planning are holding it back. Routine General spending adds 0.50 Treasury and 0.25 development points for each 1 E spent.

General is also the flexible fallback for compatible fast-track project capital and labor after the matching purpose is considered. It can therefore help different building families as the village selects work. This is its main advantage over narrowly targeted grants.

General does not directly add Food, Housing capacity or Safety in its routine conversion. If the village is hungry now, choose Food and improve farms rather than expecting General to distribute an equal share to every need. If you want to focus development on a specific family, use its matching purpose.
Food: buy time for the food supply

Routine Food spending adds 0.75 simulated Food units per 1 E spent. It raises the stock the economy uses to feed residents; it does not put edible items in chests or hand bread to individual villagers.

Food is also the matching project purpose for a Granary. That building supports agriculture, while real crops and livestock supply a separate renewable production bonus. A Food grant is useful when reserves are low or new settlers need support, but lasting farms make the benefit more sustainable.

For example, if 80 E of spendable Food funding is eventually used entirely for routine inputs, it adds 60 Food before consumption and spoilage. That is not 60 Prosperity points. Some eligible funding may instead go toward a Granary, so the Town stock is not a simple running total of your gifts.
Housing: support accommodation projects

Choose Housing when Residents exceeds Housing or when the village needs spare capacity before it can grow. Routine spending adds 0.50 Materials and 0.40 development points per 1 E spent. It does not instantly create beds or add one resident slot per emerald.

Housing is the matching purpose for Cottages, Houses and Inns. With enough eligible capital, the Fund can help the selected housing project meet its economic requirements and labor costs. The physical structure still has to be built and provide usable accommodation.

If Town reads 18 / 16, Housing is a sensible targeted contribution, but also check the beds and access already present. A blocked, distant or out-of-census-range bed may not help the immediate district. More residents require food and Safety as well as additional room.
Security: develop protection, not instant Safety points

Routine Security spending adds 0.35 Materials and 0.35 development points per 1 E spent. Its matching project is the Guard Post, which strengthens security output once operational.

The gift does not immediately raise the Safety score, spawn an iron golem, remove hostile mobs or end a raid. Those are important distinctions: a village at Safety 30 will not become Safety 100 simply because you donated 70 emeralds.

Use Security alongside work in the world. Keep villagers alive, deal with threats and light useful outdoor space. After the incident recovery window, lighting and security output help the Safety calculation recover over time. Money supports the development path; it is not a replacement for protection.
Infrastructure: materials and productive works

Routine Infrastructure spending has the same input conversion as Housing: 0.50 Materials and 0.40 development points per 1 E spent. The difference is the project family it can target.

Infrastructure matches Warehouses, Mine Entrances and Smithies. Those projects support storage-related commerce, mining and other productive activity; they are not extra Housing slots. Use this purpose when material production or the infrastructure needed for later tiers is the bottleneck.

For example, reaching tier 3 normally calls for both a Warehouse and a Mine Entrance, alongside enough residents and Prosperity. Infrastructure funding can help the economy afford that work, but it does not automatically set the tier to 3 or build every missing project at once.
Trade: support the village's economy

Routine Trade spending adds 0.65 Treasury and 0.15 development points per 1 E spent. Compared with General's routine conversion, it emphasizes the village's operating money more strongly.

Trade matches Market Squares and Exchange Halls for targeted project funding. These support the village economy and its trade output. This purpose is not the same as the GUI's Trade tab, where you sell resources into your own Bank Cash.

Choose Trade when you want to support commerce-related development or Treasury. It does not buy investment shares for you, improve all sale quotes by a fixed amount or guarantee a market return. Village outcomes and personal investment performance remain separate.
Restoration: restart an abandoned settlement

Restoration adds 1 E to the recorded restoration fund for each 1 E applied. The recovery target is 25 E. Direct grants for Abandoned or Extinct villages are treated as Restoration, and Restoration grants do not lose a share to the emergency reserve.

This purpose addresses the restoration requirement, not ordinary crowding or a single poor harvest in an Active town. Reaching 25 E marks restoration as funded; recovery still follows its timing, automatic-recovery setting and safe physical settler checks.

The interface may continue to show a recovering or empty settlement while arrivals are queued. Give it time with usable beds, food and a safe loaded area. If the desk is associated with the wrong settlement, investigate that association instead of treating additional donations as a cure.
Understand the Fund balances

Village balance (called Spendable in older screens) is purpose-budget money still available for ordinary support. It is not your personal spending balance. Reserve is pooled emergency support for situations such as critical food shortages, very low Safety or restoration. It is normally held back rather than routinely spent.

Endowment is protected principal, not money waiting to be spent in full. Received records lifetime gifts to this village, so it does not shrink when the village spends them. Sponsorship is separately earmarked for its project until consumed or rolled into a compatible purpose.

Support and the donor title describe your recorded contributions across the economy's villages, which can differ from this village's Received total. Recognition thresholds are 10 E for Village Supporter, 100 for Village Benefactor, 500 for Village Patron, 2,000 for Emerald Steward and 10,000 for Founder of Prosperity. Titles are recognition, not interest, extra votes or a growth multiplier.

Town's Treasury is another balance: the village's normal operating money from production and certain Fund conversions. A large Fund does not mean its whole amount is already Treasury. Read the selected purpose and routine spending pace when deciding why one is large and the other small.

After an accepted contribution, a receipt records the actual amount, actual purpose, sources of payment and credited allocation. It is kept for this Desk visit; the Activity log remains the bounded history of older gifts. Crediting the Fund does not place blocks immediately. The live preview also shows village-wide received, spent and remaining totals across all donors.
