Those later spending totals cannot be attributed honestly to one person's gift, and the receipt does not pretend to do so.

Requesting a fresh preview or receiving a new gift receipt clears the old document while the replacement arrives. Waiting for the server report is not confirmation of a second payment. Only an accepted receipt records a completed contribution.
A useful first contribution

Imagine an Active town with 18 residents, capacity for 16, healthy food reserves and an unfinished Guard Post. Extra Food may not solve the current crowding. A Housing grant focuses support on future accommodation; a Security grant or eligible Sponsorship supports the Guard Post; General keeps project funding more flexible.

With the default reserve setting, a 100 E non-restoration Direct Grant creates 20 E of Reserve and 80 E in its chosen spendable purpose. Those 80 E may be used gradually for routine inputs or, where eligible, toward a matching selected project's exact needs. A gift of 100 E therefore does not promise an immediate building, 100 Treasury or 100 points.

After donating, compare Town over several economic days and watch the site while its chunks are loaded. Keep food production and lighting in good shape during construction. If growth slows again, read the new bottleneck rather than repeating the same donation automatically. The goal is a settlement able to support its next step, not simply the largest possible lifetime donation number.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.acti: Use Log and News to understand changes

Log records account activity so you can connect a changed balance with a transaction. It is the first place to look after buying, selling, transferring money or giving to the Fund. A gift is an outgoing contribution, not a failed investment trade.

News gives context about the economy and the local village. A broad market event is not the same as a physical raid occurring at your current village, and a local restoration message is not a prediction about every company. Read the headline and the affected subject together.

Town and City expansion can point to a need such as food, infrastructure or treasury reserves. Use that advice as a starting point, then check the actual values and the relevant chapter. Construction details and persistent fault information also belong in debug logs; ordinary play should not require managing a list of worker tasks.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.time: Understand the clock before expecting results

One economic day follows a Minecraft day, normally about twenty real minutes at normal time progression. Rates quoted per year use 365 economic days. Production, interest, planning and recovery settle on that economic clock. Investment quotes move in smaller steps, about every fifteen real seconds during normal play; the Markets chapter explains Today, Yesterday and the longer chart ranges.

Forward changes in world time count toward economic progress. An explicit backward time command advances to the next requested sky time instead of undoing a purchase, erasing a loss or rerolling a day. For example, Day 23 midnight followed by /time set 0 becomes economic Day 24 dawn. Repeating the same sky time adds nothing. Offline progression can also be enabled and bounded in Settings; loading a world after an absence may require economic catch-up before ordinary actions resume.

Physical block placement and safe villager arrivals are different: they need loaded world space and the construction scheduler. Advancing many economic days does not instantly place every queued building. If you are testing growth, distinguish economic progress from world construction rather than repeatedly opening the GUI to make time pass.

When players sleep and the night skips forward, the missed part of that night counts once toward the economic day; it is not added again as a second day of interest or production. Recently active Banks and village construction sites also receive a bounded physical catch-up opportunity after waking, using the configured building speed to calculate skipped work.

Catch-up does not load distant chunks, create extra villagers instantly or overwrite blocked/player-owned cells. Its shared extra-work budget keeps many villages waking at once from causing one huge placement burst. At most one half-day of extra work is retained per active site, and very large time commands are capped the same way. New sites do not inherit past nights. Physical bonus credits are temporary: they expire after inactivity and are discarded on restart, disabling the mode, or changing the construction speed; the built blocks and economic progress remain saved.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.reco: When a transfer or save fails

Transfers save an inventory receipt before completing so an interruption can be recovered without guessing from the player's current item count. If a save fails, the game may disconnect you to prevent further inventory changes while that transfer is unresolved. Reconnect after a transient failure and read the message.

If inventory emeralds were safely moved to Bank Cash but the following purchase or gift failed, the completed top-up remains in cash. Check both balances before trying again; the money was moved, not deleted. Do not try to force a refund by restoring only your inventory file.

Persistent recovery errors need the server owner and a consistent backup. Old pending transfers without receipts, contradictory saves or storage failures may need manual review. The mod deliberately retains unresolved records instead of inventing a result that could duplicate or remove legitimate items.

Back up the whole world before updating or experimenting with debug settings. Keep client and server mod versions matched, do not leave two TES JAR versions installed, and do not downgrade a save with pending transactions. A whole-world backup keeps player inventory and the economy from being restored to different moments.

When reporting a problem, include the version and source fingerprint displayed at the bottom of a Town or Fund report. Both loader builds expose this identity in debug captures too. It identifies the compiled source candidate, not your private world. Use matching client/server builds and keep a full world backup before updating. A matching save format does not make older binaries safe for downgrades.

For a performance test, an operator can run /emerald debug, reproduce the slowdown while staying near the work, then run it again to save the ZIP. The default capture lasts five real minutes if you do not stop it. Keep a normal-play capture as a baseline before comparing forced instant development. Sleeping or using /time does not invent tick samples or postpone the performance sampling clock.

Open performance-summary.json for server milliseconds per tick (MSPT): the capture-wide mean and maximum, counts over 50, 100 and 250 milliseconds, and exact p50, p95 and p99 values for the most recent 1,200 measured ticks. At a normal 20 TPS, each tick has a 50-millisecond budget. A low average can hide occasional long spikes, so compare the maximum, percentiles and slow-tick counts too. No completed samples means unavailable, not zero lag.

Observed ticks per second uses completed samples divided by real elapsed capture time, not 1,000 divided by MSPT. Pauses and unusually fast tick settings affect that result; configured tick rate, frozen and sprinting states are included. Measurements cover server tick work including construction and recorder callbacks, not client FPS or a claim that TES alone caused a slowdown. The older recorder/write/copy timings still describe debug overhead separately. The first and last partial capture ticks are excluded.

Construction counts separate all saved unfinished projects, placed versus unplaced projects, pending Bank sites and sites recently working or waiting. A site that placed blocks and then began waiting can appear in both recent counts. Recent observations cover five real seconds and at most 2,048 tracked sites; a loaded-looking or queued site is not proof it is doing work now. Completed and abstract projects are kept separate. Counts do not force-load chunks or scan world blocks. timeline.jsonl pairs timing and workload snapshots about once per real second while server ticks continue, making it easier to connect spikes with construction activity. Share the capture with what you changed and whether the problem was smooth slowdown or occasional freezes.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.bank: A desk is access, not the village itself

The low stair blocks on a Bank's front terrace are decorative benches. Newly planned Banks turn their seats toward the front path, with their raised backs toward the building. They do not add a sitting interaction. Existing completed Banks keep their original blocks; you can turn the seats yourself after construction if you prefer.

An Exchange Desk lets you reach your personal account. A verified village Bank and its Banker have additional local operation requirements. If the building is not currently verified, the desk may open personal banking access with a warning rather than treating the Bank as operational.

Town and Fund depend on the settlement associated with the access point. If a distant Bank says Abandoned while a desk in the village shows many residents, that is an association or census issue worth reporting, not evidence that your account needs another deposit. Include both desk coordinates and which settlement each reports.

Breaking the desk, adding more desks, donating repeatedly or rebuilding the Bank elsewhere is not a safe general repair procedure. Keep the world backup, allow loaded census updates, and collect a debug report when the disagreement persists. Your personal balance should be the same across desks even when their local Town information differs.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.paus:
A disabled button can mean the selected action has no valid source, the exact amount is too large, a term or project is missing, or the economy is still catching up. Check the preview and tooltip before assuming the interface has lost your emeralds. Ordinary loose inventory emeralds count for spending; customized items and nested storage do not.

If City expansion is waiting, check its reason. A maturing district needs sustained health and development, not merely one high Prosperity reading. A food, material or upkeep warning calls for the relevant supply. A newly founded district may still be establishing its first home.

World settings can disable simulation, visual progression, donations or particular funding types. Paused expansion and forced debug development are different controls. In single player the settings editor applies to the current world; on a remote server the server owner controls world behavior. Hover a setting label, toggle or number field for its explanation and allowed range. Long help text wraps onto readable lines; keyboard-focused controls also show help. Financial previews keep their exact amounts, fees and penalties. Reset restores defaults, while unapplied edits are not a reason to expect the server to behave differently.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.reci:
The bundled default recipe uses a crafting table. Place an emerald in the top middle, leather on either side of a book in the middle row, and matching planks across the bottom row. Different valid plank types can be mixed.

Place the resulting desk and right-click it for account access. The recipe preview is teaching you the ingredients, not crafting them for you. Hover to pause the cycling ingredients and read item names, or use Pause recipes. Server datapacks can change recipes; pay attention to whether the card says a known server recipe or a default recipe.

To build against the desk, crouch and right-click while holding a placeable block in your main hand or offhand. Minecraft handles the placement and consumes the block normally in Survival. Ordinary right-click still opens banking, including when you are holding a block. A blocked placement leaves the desk closed; it does not spend the item.

Craft one book and one emerald together in any two slots to make another Starter Handbook. Their positions do not matter: the cycling preview demonstrates a shapeless recipe, not several different costs.

Use the handbook to open this reader. Search can find topics inside chapters as well as their titles; A- and A+ change reader text size, and the body scrolls when a chapter is longer than the screen. Replacing the book does not reset your account, discoveries or village progress.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.glos: Balances and principal

Bank Cash is the account balance available to spend or withdraw. Inventory emeralds are physical items that can also cover GUI spending. Savings is a separate liquid, interest-bearing balance; it must return to cash before ordinary spending.

Principal means the original sum placed into a financial product. Net Worth is the recorded account value, excluding loose items and final gifts. Moving emeralds into the account changes that value without creating investment profit.
Rates, terms and maturity

An annual rate uses a 365-economic-day year. It is not the amount paid each day. Interest is value earned over time, while the term is the number of economic days a product is intended to run.

Maturity is the end of that term. A CD fixes its opening rate until then; Savings has a variable rate. Compare the penalty and access rules as well as the displayed rate before choosing where to put money.
Yield and default

Yield describes a quoted lending return, not a guarantee that the borrower will pay it. Default means the expected repayment failed.

A recovery rate is the share returned after a partial default. A full default may return nothing. These losses affect the money you lent; they do not make you a debtor. A Village Fund gift has no promised repayment to default on in the first place.
Assets, shares and tickers

An asset is a market investment. Shares are the units you own, including fractions. A ticker such as GLDH is its short identifier; the company name and sector explain what you are selecting.

An index is a basket-style investment rather than a single business. A commodity is a quoted resource used in trading. Owning shares in a mining company is not the same as owning a diamond item or selling ore through Trade.
Quotes, spreads and volatility

A quote is the current estimate for a trade. The spread is a trading cost between buying and selling, so an immediate round trip can lose money even with an unchanged headline price.

Volatility describes how strongly prices move, not which direction comes next. The regime is the economy's broad condition, such as expansion or recession. A risk label summarizes exposure; it is not an insurance policy against losses.
Cost basis and allocation

Cost basis is the purchase cost assigned to the position you still hold. Selling part of a holding also removes the corresponding portion of that basis. Average buy price divides the remaining basis by the remaining shares.

Allocation describes how much of your account value sits in a particular holding. A position can become a larger allocation because its price rose, not only because you bought more. The account does not count loose inventory items in those portfolio values.
Profit versus money moved

Unrealized gain or loss is the result on a position you still own. Realized gain or loss records an exit that has occurred. Neither is the same as the gross proceeds of selling: some proceeds are simply your original purchase cost coming back.

A contribution moves value in; a withdrawal or final gift moves it out. Compare transaction history with performance before treating a deposit as a gain or a donation as a market loss.
Gift budgets

A Direct Grant supplies current support, usually split between its purpose and an emergency reserve. An Endowment preserves principal and releases payouts over time. Sponsorship earmarks a gift for a selected project's economic labor.

Purpose selects a spending route and matching project family. It is not a direct purchase of Prosperity, Safety or housing points. The Village Fund chapter explains each route and gives conversion examples.
Village money and donor recognition

Treasury is ordinary village operating money. Spendable purpose budgets, Reserve and Endowment are separate Fund balances. Received is a lifetime record, not the amount left to spend today.

A donor title recognizes your cumulative contributions. It does not give you ownership of the village, withdrawable shares, extra interest or a financial advantage. Your support total and one village's lifetime receipts can differ.
Town measurements

Prosperity is a 0-to-100 living-conditions score; Safety is a separate stability score. Housing is effective resident capacity. Development tier is a functional level from 0 to 5, while development points are an internal planning input.

Food and Materials are simulated stocks. F / M / T are Farm, Mine and Trade outputs, not counts of buildings or inventory stacks. Production, consumption and upkeep explain why output is not the same as net daily growth.
Projects, districts and lifecycle

Planning is economic project work; Building is visible placement in the loaded world. A backlog is work awaiting physical construction. Economic completion and the building you can see are therefore not always at the same stage.

Lifecycle describes the settlement's condition, such as Active, Threatened or Recovering. New natural villages have one district: its connected territory grows with approved building sites, not by creating more neighborhoods and Banks. Nearby natural villages remain separate. Upkeep is the continuing cost of residents and facilities. Legacy multi-district cities retain their administration costs; neither a high tier nor a large donation removes those costs.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.grow: Positive prospects are not promised returns

Stocks and commodities have a slowly changing, positive underlying annual growth target between 1%% and 15%%. This is a game-balance assumption about business prospects or long-run resource value, not interest paid to your account. An economic year is 365 economic days. Actual yearly returns can be negative or exceed 15%%; there is no year-end catch-up payment or guaranteed recovery.

The base sampling weights favor 1-4%% (70%%), then 4-8%% (23%%), 8-12%% (6%%), and 12-15%% (1%%). The model blends successive samples smoothly over 181 days, so those weights describe sampled endpoints, not exact time spent in each band. Coal and diamonds favor lower prospects, while copper, redstone and some growth businesses lean higher. Reloading cannot reroll the world-seeded path.

Companies share broad economic conditions but retain their own prospects, industry behavior and risks. VILX tracks all twelve companies by simulated market capitalization. Its indicative fundamental bias is the weighted average of their targets, within 1-15%%, not its own draw. Averaging and drifting concentration change the target distribution; actual performance is not guaranteed. TREA remains a rate-sensitive treasury fund. Savings and CD interest rules are unchanged. Positive prospects do not cancel recessions, supply shocks or bad company outcomes.

Commodity reference values grow gradually, while market prices fluctuate around supply-and-demand conditions. Normal annual volatility settings are Gold 18%%, Iron 32%%, Coal 45%%, Diamond 22%%, Copper 28%%, Redstone 35%%, Lapis 25%% and Netherite Scrap 40%%. Turbulent periods temporarily increase volatility. These are noise settings, not return promises or loss limits. Rarity can raise a price and magnify a shortage without guaranteeing the best investment return.

Older saves keep their current prices, units, cash and recorded history. New commodity reference values start from the existing quotes. Physical Trade and commodity investments still share the same underlying price, so opening another tab does not create an arbitrage route.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.news:
Craft a Village Newspaper from one paper and one ink sac, in any two crafting slots. Look for the rolled grey newspaper with black print, a paper band and a curled end. While you read the portable paper, that held copy unfolds into a pocket gazette with a folded corner, village illustration and printed columns. Closing the reader rolls it up again. Other copies, dropped papers and the Exchange Desk browser remain rolled. This changes only its appearance; it does not consume paper, create another item or change saved item data. Use the newspaper anywhere to open The Emerald Wire. It is reusable, free to read and opens news only, not remote banking. Desk > News > Read The Emerald Wire opens the searchable network browser.

The portable paper opens as a newspaper, with a masthead, lead story, bylines and two-column reading. Recent significant events lead ahead of routine roundups; old events gradually move down the edition. Read the lead or another headline, or use Next from the cover to begin a continuous reading route: front page, every Contents sheet, then all stories in editorial order. Contents labels each story by number and lets you jump directly to it; these are story numbers, not promises that every report fits on one page. Front page returns to the cover.

The mouse wheel scrolls through a long report, then continues into the next story when you scroll again at its end. Next advances a full two-column view before moving on to another story, so it does not skip unread text. Previous and upward scrolling reverse the same route, arriving at the end of the preceding report. Navigation stops only at the beginning or end of the entire edition. The footer shows your story and visible text range.

The masthead is simply The Emerald Wire. Faint paper fibres, folds and a small margin tear add texture behind the ink without changing the reports or reducing reading space. The paper never changes account balances.

The Exchange Desk keeps the channel-style archive. Choose All, Markets, Local, Players or Community, then search or cycle outlets. Search covers up to 256 retained reports, not only the visible page. Both views read the same published facts, but the item prioritizes reading while the Desk prioritizes finding a report.

New stories wait behind the New stories! button so an incoming edition cannot silently replace what you are reading. Accepting preserves the selected article if it is still retained. Unread stars last for this reader visit; privacy restrictions take effect immediately on synchronization even if you have not accepted a new edition.

The Emerald Ledger focuses on financial analysis, The Redstone Wire on technology, The Nether Post on trade routes, and The Overworld Observer on communities. The Daily Gravel labels its opinion and satire. Editorial voices interpret the same measured facts; they do not apply extra price effects.

Follow-ups revisit market prices relative to their pre-event level after two and seven economic days. This is not proof that a shortage has ended. Local follow-ups can report changed simulated food estimates, explicitly distinguished from physical repairs. Observed replanting or restocking can continue a village story without claiming every loss was fixed.

The archive reserves room for Markets, Local, Players and Community while borrowing unused space. Developing stories are tracked separately, so player-report bursts cannot cancel market follow-ups. Repetitive actions by the same player, village and category merge into a daily bulletin. Wording is finite, seeded and repeat-aware. Operators can override validated wording through data packs and /reload; past published facts are not rewritten.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.play: When your actions make the paper

The local paper can report observed food removal, crop and building-block removal, confirmed player-caused villager deaths, significant Fund gifts, replanting and restocking. These are observations, not proof of malicious intent or permission agreements. Removing food is not automatically called theft, and rearranging a building is not proof of wrongdoing.

Ordinary reporting uses existing village structure evidence and recorded player placements. Unknown ownership or automation is not enough to name a player. Older unrecorded modifications can be ambiguous. For stricter worlds, operators can enable News: explicit property only and designate community block positions with /emerald news property add <from x y z> <to x y z>. Use remove with the same coordinates to revoke it. A designation permits reporting, not construction, and changes no blocks. Limit: 4096 positions per command, 16384 per dimension; a managed nearby village is still required.

Food clicks have a ten-second net observation window: taking food and returning it cancels out, and at least eight items must remain removed or added. Crops allow two minutes of game ticks for replanting; unloaded observations wait. At least four removed structure blocks are needed for a damage bulletin. Creative and Spectator block/container actions are excluded. Fund gifts of at least 64 E may receive positive coverage.

World settings control public player reports, anonymous names, exact location disclosure and explicit-only property evidence. By default exact district coordinates are withheld; anonymous names are optional. Disabling public reports stops new local reporting and hides retained local articles from readers, without deleting the private server archive. These settings cannot erase information another player already saw or recorded.

A player's same-category actions within one economic day update the same bulletin. Observed restocking and replanting can be linked to an earlier village report. Food follow-ups describe the Town simulation estimate, not proof that stolen supplies were returned or every crop was restored. News creates no fine, guard hostility, extra global price shock or inventory transfer.

Tracking remains bounded and loaded-only. Capacity limits can cause a report to be skipped rather than perform unlimited work. Observation windows and articles persist, but a machine crash before saving can lose the last moments of activity.
guide.the_emerald_standard.handbook.reci:

Additional copies show the same reports rather than generating extra events. The Exchange Desk's News tab offers a searchable browser of the same reports. A newspaper is a news item, not a portable Exchange Desk; accounts and transactions still use their existing access rules.
